lead: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — Truth Social launches on a closed market
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — digital gold flunks the weekend war test
Tesla / TSLA — Musk picks a fight with the SEC
Gold Miners ETF / GDX — the old haven still earns its keep
why_lead: Truth Social's App Store release was a dated pending catalyst for Monday 21 February (Reuters n0932, Axios n1766), landing on a US market holiday, with saturation-level mainstream coverage as the attention evidence (Newsweek n1723, Vanity Fair n1744, Snopes rumour check n1755, Reuters testers n1742, Forbes n1722). DWAC closed at 84.32 USD on 18 February, +15.32% over 20 sessions and +2.83% over five against a falling Nasdaq 100 (-1.14%) and Robinhood (-11.34% 5s), a simple repeatable buy-the-rumour story. Nunes's end-of-March full-operation timetable (n1765) and the Virgin Galactic round trip (n0523 surge, n0903 Palihapitiya exit, SPCE 5s -0.47%) supply the break and the analog. Relation to strictly earlier retail notes (1-16 February): DWAC/Truth Social was never a lead or smaller item; Virgin Galactic was a 16 February smaller item on the $450,000 ticket relaunch, and it is used here only as an analog updated with the newly published 18 February Palihapitiya resignation and the round-tripped price. The launch outcome itself is after the cutoff and is not used.
why_smaller: Bitcoin: the weekend's only open market fell 4.21% on 20 February and 13.78% over five sessions, Ether -17.33%, as Buterin welcomed another winter (Bloomberg n1001) and the Super Bowl ad blitz (Bloomberg n0360) met reports that the ad millions did not drive downloads (Seattle Times n0086); US-listed proxies (MARA, COIN) had yet to price the slide. Relation to earlier notes: Bitcoin led on 8 and 14 February (crypto spring, Super Bowl recruitment), was a smaller item on 4 and 9 February and Coinbase led on 15 February; this is a brief secondary material update (the post-ad hangover and a 13.78% weekly drop, with evidence published 16-19 February), framed as digital gold failing the war test while gold rose.

Tesla: a new narrative for the month, retail loyalty to a founder in a fight with the SEC (Reuters n0736, Forbes n1851) and a returning short-seller despite low short interest (Teslarati n1711), against TSLA 856.98 USD, -2.21% on 18 February and -9.21% over 20 sessions; breaks on the braking probe (Reuters n1867) and the Boombox recall (NPR n1866). Tesla was not an item in earlier retail notes. It replaced an ARK Innovation ETF dip-faith item after the 1 February note showed ARKK had already run as 'Cathie's faithful buy the deepest dip'.

GDX: the safe-haven war trade, gold 1,899.80 USD/oz (+3.13% 5s) and GDX +6.38% 5s, refreshed by newly published catalysts after the 14 February GDX item ('the invasion hedge with leverage'): Biden saying he was convinced Putin had decided to invade (BBC n1424), Putin overseeing nuclear drills (n1422) and the extension of the Belarus drills (n1435); breaks on the Macron summit track (n1430) or rate pressure (n1776). Kept secondary as a material update.
considered_not_chosen: ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK -4.96% on 18 February, -9.87% 5s; Cathie Wood n1741, n1757; Bloomberg n1720): new statements, but the narrative repeats the 1 February smaller item almost word for word, so replaced by Tesla.

DraftKings (DKNG -21.62% on 18 February, -25.89% 5s): largest 1-session drop on the card, but no own-date headline on its results beyond a generic sports-betting-margins piece (n1119), so no supportable catalyst or attention evidence.
Upstart (UPST +30.02% 5s, -6.86% 1s): big post-results swing but only a generic 'is now a good time to scoop up' piece (n0576).
Roblox and Shopify post-earnings crashes (n0117, n0631, n0640): Roblox was a 16 February smaller item; no new catalyst after its results.
Defense stocks (ITA -0.84% 5s, LMT -2.46% 5s): no war-trade rally on the card yet.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff or misdated: n1427 and n1440 (Biden agreeing in principle to meet Putin, a White House statement that may post-date 00:00 UTC 21 February), n1319 (CNN 'Photos: Russia invades Ukraine', stamped 14 February, misdated), Reuters LIVE MARKETS blogs (n1274, n1264, n1229, n1218).
